sources.title: Final report of the Group of Experts on the DRC (S/2024/969)
Final report of the Group of Experts on the DRC (S/2025/446)
sources.notes: Para 120: RDB claims 8,000-9,000 t/yr 3T, contradicted by NISR, geology and ITSCI. Para 115: >500 t 3T looted in Goma/Bukavu + 186 t Nyabibwe. Para 118: 195 t in one week, Mar 2025. Annex 53: BGR geology puts coltan at ~25% of mixed coltan-cassiterite deposits; RDB implied 60-70%; not all 2024 Rwandan tantalite exports could come from domestic production.

sources.title: Who buys Rwanda's smuggled coltan?
sources.notes: Partner imports from Rwanda >2,900 t coltan in 2024 (matches our Comtrade mirror 2,909 t). China imported 1,571 t (2023) and 2,286 t (2024). ITSCI tantalite share of tagged 3T exports rose from 21% (2020) to 31% (2024). Official coltan exports up >2.5x 2021-2025. Web summary also read: globalwitness.org/en/campaigns/transition-minerals/who-buys-rwandas-smuggled-coltan-...

Per MONTH, not per year: AFC/M23 controlled trade and transport of ~120 t coltan monthly from Rubaya, mid-May to late Oct 2024 (para 64). Annex 29 says 150 t/month smuggled from Rubaya to Rwanda. MONUSCO: conservative 100 t/month produced in Rubaya (fn 67).
Annual: ~400 t coltan from PE4731 (Rubaya) smuggled into the legal chain via PE76 in 2023 (annex 29). Cross-site smuggling inside DRC, not to Rwanda.

conversions.notes: Low: USGS assumption 26% Ta2O5 x 0.81897 Ta in Ta2O5 = 0.213 t Ta per t concentrate. High: implied ratio in USGS 2024 table, 300 t Ta / 1,300 t concentrate. Actual Rwandan grades vary; not measured.
MCS generic assumption for US trade: tantalum ores 32% Ta2O5 x 0.81897 = 0.262. Not Rwanda-specific; shown for comparison only.
USGS: domestically mined cassiterite averaged 63% Sn (2024). Implied 4,100/6,485 = 0.632.
Implied by USGS W-content / gross rows (2018-2024 range ~0.44-0.48). USGS text gives 66-70% "tungsten content" at Nyakabingo, likely WO3 grade (WO3 is 79.3% W) rather than W; not used.

caveats: USGS coltan and tungsten 'production' for Rwanda is Rwanda's reported export tonnage (USGS footnote 'Reported exports'). Using it as the production side makes the gap zero by construction. For coltan 2023-24, USGS holds an estimate at 1,300 t while exports were 2,070 t and 2,384 t.

No independent, mineral-specific estimate of Rwanda's production capacity was found in open sources. production_estimate_low/high are null. The only 3T total is Rwanda's own RDB claim of 8,000-9,000 t/yr, which the UN Group of Experts says NISR data, geology and ITSCI records contradict. 2025 3T exports (Comtrade: 2,743 + 6,349 + 3,009 = ~12,100 t) exceed even that claim.

Rwanda-reported Comtrade figures and BNR official figures are the same dataset (identical to the kg for coltan and tungsten), so they are not independent confirmation. Mirror data (partner imports) is the only independent export series.
BNR 'Cassiterite' exceeds Comtrade HS 260900 every year from 2019 (e.g. 2024: 4,861 t vs 4,018 t). The cause is unresolved and may be tin metal from the Kigali smelter or a scope difference.

Mirror coltan has anomalies. Malaysia reports 2,083 t (2021) and 1,898 t (2025) at ~$4-5/kg, implausible for coltan and probably misclassified tin slag or similar. 2025 mirror data covers only China and Malaysia. Use China's mirror (1,571 t 2023; 2,286 t 2024; 2,865 t 2025) as the cleanest single series.

Gold: exports (~19.4 t in 2024, $1.5bn, almost all to UAE) dwarf USGS mine output (~0.35 t Au/yr). However, Rwanda imports and refines large amounts of gold (USGS: gold was 26.6% of 2024 imports), so the gold gap mixes declared re-exports with any laundering. Comtrade 2025 Rwanda gold exports fell to 6.4 t ($519m). UAE has not reported 2024-25 imports, so no mirror is available.
Units: exports are gross concentrate weight (kg). USGS contained-metal figures need the conversion factors above, which are assumptions (26% Ta2O5 etc.), not measured grades.

Comtrade Rwanda-reported partner rows include transit and trading hubs (Luxembourg = code 442, likely Traxys; Hong Kong; UAE; Singapore; Switzerland). These are traders' domiciles, not processing destinations. Trade data shows who shipped and who received, not where ore was mined.
The BNR file ends in July 2025, so BNR 2025 values cover 7 months. Comtrade 2025 is full-year as reported by Rwanda.

Any gap computed from these numbers is 'inferred' (our analysis) and must be labelled as such. A gap is consistent with smuggled DRC material but does not prove it. Stock drawdowns, grade differences and data errors are alternatives. Rwanda denies supporting M23 and denies laundering.
